sources: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK482316/
Standard O₂ transport physiology — CaO₂ = (1.34 × Hb × SaO₂) + (0.003 × PaO₂); content term in DO₂ = CO × CaO₂; restrictive transfusion thresholds for stable ICU anemia
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK564395/
Mixed venous (PA) content for Fick/AV O₂ difference/O₂ER; ScvO₂/central venous content used as bedside surrogate
https://litfl.com/oxygen-extraction-ratio/
O₂ER ≈ 20–30% normal; rises with low DO₂ or high VO₂ (low SvO₂); low O₂ER/high SvO₂ in shock suggests distributive shock or impaired utilization
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9727764/
Paret et al. Pediatr Pulmonol 1998 — VI = RR × (PIP−PEEP) × PaCO₂ / 1000; classically pediatric respiratory-failure intensity metric
https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJM199105233242101
Yang & Tobin NEJM 1991 — f/Vt; RSBI <105 breaths/min/L associated with weaning success; combine with successful SBT for extubation planning
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10793162/
ARDSNet ARMA — Vt dosed by PBW (height/sex), not actual weight; ~6 mL/kg PBW; Pplat ≤30 cm H₂O; PEEP/FiO₂ tables
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10793162/
ARMA: 6 vs 12 mL/kg PBW reduced ARDS mortality; if Pplat >30 reduce Vt toward 4 mL/kg PBW
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25693014/
Amato et al. NEJM 2015 — ΔP (Pplat−PEEP) strongly associated with ARDS mortality; clinical aim often ≤15 cm H₂O when feasible
https://litfl.com/compliance/
Cstat = Vt/(Pplat−PEEP) requires passive patient and reliable plateau; falling Cstat → edema, fibrosis, mainstem tube, abdominal hypertension, pneumothorax
https://litfl.com/airway-resistance/
Raw from (PIP−Pplat)/flow on passive constant-flow volume breath; high Raw → ETT, secretions, bronchospasm; manage auto-PEEP with expiratory time
https://derangedphysiology.com/main/cicm-primary-exam/respiratory-system/Chapter-034/time-constants
τ = Raw × C; ~3 time constants empty ~95% of VT; long τ + auto-PEEP → lower rate, longer expiration, bronchodilation, permissive hypercapnia
https://www.ombudsman.org.uk/sites/default/files/National_Early_Warning_Score_%28NEWS%29_-_Standardising_the_assessment_of_acute-illness_severity_in_the_NHS_0.pdf
RCP original NEWS — aggregate ≥7 emergency/critical-care response; 5–6 or single parameter score 3 = urgent review (NEWS2 later de-emphasized lone red score)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19794327/
Gaies et al. 2010 — VIS quantifies vasoactive/inotrope intensity (pediatric cardiac ICU classic; adult research use)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20179283/
Jones et al. JAMA 2010 — ≥10% lactate clearance as early sepsis resuscitation goal comparator; poor clearance/rising lactate → reassess perfusion and source
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3411642/
Davis et al. J Trauma 1988 — BD correlates with volume need/mortality in trauma; treat shock source; avoid bicarbonate-only focus
https://chemm.hhs.gov/triage.htm
SALT (Sort-Assess-Lifesaving interventions-Treatment/transport) — CDC-sponsored; MUCC-aligned (NHTSA/EMS national framework); categories Immediate/Delayed/Minimal/Expectant/Dead
https://chemm.hhs.gov/jumpstartalgotext.htm
JumpSTART — pediatric MCI triage; RR 15–45 band; airway positioning + rescue breaths if pulse present; modifies START for pediatric physiology
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15857740/
Nu-DESC — brief nurse observational screen; score ≥2 positive → formal assessment (CAM-ICU/ICDSC) and reversible-cause workup
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10470756/
Riker SAS — validated ICU sedation scale; light targets often SAS 3–4; PADIS: minimize deep sedation, SAT/SBT, treat pain/delirium causes of agitation
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11430542/
ICDSC — shift-based ICU delirium checklist; ≥4 delirium; 1–3 often labeled subsyndromal; nonpharm bundle; avoid benzos unless withdrawal
https://www.ahrq.gov/patient-safety/settings/hospital/resource/pressureulcer/tool/pu7b.html
Braden — widely used NA pressure-injury risk tool; total ≤18 generally at risk (ICU cutoffs may differ); support surface, reposition, moisture/nutrition, heel offload
https://www.cgakit.com/waterlow-score
Waterlow — UK tool; ≥10 at risk, 15–19 high, ≥20 very high; build/skin/sex-age/continence/mobility/nutrition/special risks
https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/multimedia/table/the-norton-scale-for-predicting-pressure-ulcer-risk
Norton 5-item scale; ≤14 (or <14) commonly flags increased pressure-injury risk
https://www.bapen.org.uk/pdfs/must/must_full.pdf
BAPEN MUST — 0 low risk routine rescreen; 1 medium monitor intake ~3 days; ≥2 high risk dietitian/nutrition care plan
